When testing the API-X demo[1] depositing binaries via the Fedora html UI, sometimes the user is redirected to the wrong place.  Instead of /fcr:metadata, the user is sometimes directed to the API-X service document.
This appears to be due to the UI parsing link headers incorrectly.  If there are multiple link relations, e.g.:
Link: </otherPlace>; rel="anOtherRel"
Link: </fcr:metadata>; rel="describedby"
.. the net effect is that the UI picks a random link regardless of relation.
Chrome browser

fields.summary: UI does not parse Link headers correctly when redirecting

comments.body:
This seems to be a javascript issue in:

const fn = function (method, url, headers, data) {
      http(method, url, headers, data, function(res) {
        if (res.status == 201) {
          const loc = res.getResponseHeader('Location');
          const link = res.getResponseHeader('Link');
          if (link != null && link.match('rel="describedby"')) {
            const str = link.match(/<[^>]+>/)[0];
            window.location = str.slice(1, str.length - 1);
          } else if (loc != null) {
            window.location = loc;
          } else {
            window.location.reload();
          }
        } else {
            ajaxErrorHandler(res, 'Error creating binary');
        }
      });

According to Mozilla if there is more than one header with the same name, all headers are returned in a single comma separated string.

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/XMLHttpRequest/getResponseHeader

On second thought trying to test this through a docker machine is too confusing. However I think the answer is much the same as Unknown did for the checkIfNonRdfResource so something like

    const fn = function (method, url, headers, data) {
      http(method, url, headers, data, function(res) {
        if (res.status == 201) {
          const loc = res.getResponseHeader('Location');
          const linkheaders = res.getResponseHeader('Link').split(", ");
          const link = linkheaders.filter(function(h) { return h.match(/rel="describedby"/)});
          if (linkheaders != null && link.length > 0) {
            window.location = link[0].substr(1, link[0].indexOf('>') - 1);
          } else if (loc != null) {
            window.location = loc;
          } else {
            window.location.reload();
          }
        } else {
            ajaxErrorHandler(res, 'Error creating binary');
        }
      });
    }

should work.

@awoods I don't receive a null on my platform. I've tried this patch against master and against 4.7.1. I'm using Chrome on Mac OS version 56.0.2924.87 (64-bit).

The other platform I have available to test on is Safari version 9.1.2 (11601.7.7), but that just seems totally broken (unrelated to this patch).

I pushed an update that I hope guards against null objects. Please test and let me know if it works for you.
